problem: Coarse accuracy is stated flatly as 'about a kilometre'. A coarse fix is usually a Wi-Fi/cell-tower estimate, so it can be a few hundred metres (several Wi-Fi networks seen) up to one or two kilometres (single cell tower). The single figure may be taken as a guaranteed value.
fix: ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION gives an approximate fix — from a few hundred metres up to one or two kilometres, depending on whether Wi-Fi or only a cell tower was used. Fine is metres level.

problem: The formula lists an 'expiration' argument but never says what it means or what value to pass. A student cannot use the call from this description.
fix: Add: expiration is the lifetime of the alert in milliseconds, after which it is removed automatically; pass -1 for an alert that never expires.

problem: The text says to call Geocoder off the main thread but does not say that the geocoding service may be absent, so the call fails on some devices and emulators.
fix: Add: check Geocoder.isPresent() first; if it is false, the device has no geocoding backend and the app must fall back or hide the feature.

problem: The answer 'about 1.4 per minute' is an average rate, but the question asks how many updates arrive per minute. A student may read it as 'two fixes in one minute', when in the first minute after starting from rest only one fix arrives (at about 41.7 s).
fix: State it as a rate: fixes come about every 41.7 s, that is about 1.4 per minute on average; in the first 60 s from a standing start only one fix is delivered.
